---
title: "svelte/no-reactive-literals"
description: "Don't assign literal values in reactive statements"
# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.

A `$:` statement that assigns a literal, an empty array or an empty object depends on nothing, so it never runs again. A plain `let` does the same. The suggestion replaces the statement with `let` and the assignment. The rule looks at components that are not in runes mode.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-reactive-literals": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  $: items = [];
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  let items = [];
</script>
```
